just kids.title: Just Kids
just kids.author: Patti Smith
just kids.why: The singer's tender memoir of her friendship with Robert Mapplethorpe in 1970s New York; moving and beautifully written.

catcher in the rye.title: The Catcher in the Rye
catcher in the rye.author: J. D. Salinger
catcher in the rye.why: A teenage boy wanders New York after leaving school; a short coming-of-age classic readers still enjoy.

sharp objects.title: Sharp Objects
sharp objects.author: Gillian Flynn
sharp objects.why: A reporter returns to her hometown to cover murders and confronts her family; a gripping, disturbing thriller.

things fall apart.title: Things Fall Apart
things fall apart.author: Chinua Achebe
things fall apart.why: A proud Igbo man's world is upended by colonisers; short and powerful, often read as an answer to colonial fiction.

good omens.title: Good Omens
good omens.author: Terry Pratchett
good omens.why: An angel and a demon try to stop the apocalypse because they like Earth; hilarious and widely loved.

stranger in a strange land.title: Stranger in a Strange Land
stranger in a strange land.author: Robert A. Heinlein
stranger in a strange land.why: A human raised by Martians returns to Earth and shakes up its customs; a famous, provocative counterculture classic.

child of god.title: Child of God
child of god.author: Cormac McCarthy
child of god.why: A violent outcast lives in the Tennessee hills; short and harrowing, for readers who can handle disturbing McCarthy.

meditations.title: Meditations
meditations.author: Marcus Aurelius
meditations.why: The Roman emperor's private notes on duty, calm and death; readers value its practical stoic advice.

immortal life of henrietta lacks.title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
immortal life of henrietta lacks.author: Rebecca Skloot
immortal life of henrietta lacks.why: The story of the woman whose cells were taken without consent and used in science; moving and informative.

candide.title: Candide
candide.author: Voltaire
candide.why: A naive young man travels through disaster after disaster while told that all is for the best; short and biting.

butter.title: Butter
butter.author: Asako Yuzuki
butter.why: A journalist becomes obsessed with a gourmet woman convicted of murder; food, gender and appetite make it hard to stop.

shark heart.title: Shark Heart
shark heart.author: Emily Habeck
shark heart.why: A man is slowly turning into a shark as his wife prepares to lose him; strange, tender and loved by readers.

curse of chalion.title: The Curse of Chalion
curse of chalion.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
curse of chalion.why: A broken soldier becomes tutor to a princess in a kingdom cursed by gods; deeply human and well liked.

blade itself.title: The Blade Itself
blade itself.author: Joe Abercrombie
blade itself.why: A torturer, a barbarian and a vain swordsman are drawn into a war; grim and funny, the start of The First Law.

you.title: You
you.author: Caroline Kepnes
you.why: A bookstore clerk stalks a woman and tells it as love; creepy, addictive thriller.

assassins apprentice.title: Assassin's Apprentice
assassins apprentice.author: Robin Hobb
assassins apprentice.why: A royal bastard is trained as a secret killer; slow-building and emotional, the first Farseer book.

nothing to see here.title: Nothing to See Here
nothing to see here.author: Kevin Wilson
nothing to see here.why: A woman becomes nanny to two children who burst into flames; absurd, warm and quick, making readers laugh out loud.

mrs dalloway.title: Mrs. Dalloway
mrs dalloway.author: Virginia Woolf
mrs dalloway.why: One day in the life of a London woman and a shell-shocked soldier; stream of consciousness that some love.

scanner darkly.title: A Scanner Darkly
scanner darkly.author: Philip K. Dick
scanner darkly.why: An undercover agent addicted to a drug watches himself; paranoid and sad, someone's comfort book.

finnegans wake.title: Finnegans Wake
finnegans wake.author: James Joyce
finnegans wake.why: The comments describe it as unread or too hard, not recommended.

corrections.title: The Corrections
corrections.author: Jonathan Franzen
corrections.why: A midwestern family comes together for a last Christmas; funny and moving, though compared to DeLillo.

collector.title: The Collector
collector.author: John Fowles
collector.why: A lonely man kidnaps a young woman and keeps her in his cellar; a short, chilling psychological novel.

midnights children.title: Midnight's Children
midnights children.author: Salman Rushdie
midnights children.why: A man born at India's independence is linked to other children with powers; colourful and demanding magical realism.

ice.title: Ice
ice.author: Anna Kavan
ice.why: A narrator chases a girl through a world freezing under ice; short, dreamlike and experimental.

player of games.title: The player of games
player of games.author: Iain Banks
player of games.why: A game master is sent to play an alien empire's brutal game; a smart and approachable Culture novel.

hunger.title: Hunger
hunger.author: Knut Hamsun
hunger.why: The comments mix up several books titled Hunger, so there is no clear recommendation for this one.

howls moving castle.title: Howl's Moving Castle
howls moving castle.author: Diana Wynne Jones
howls moving castle.why: A girl turned into an old woman moves into a wizard's castle; funny and charming, different from the film.

dawn.title: Dawn
dawn.author: Octavia E. Butler
dawn.why: Aliens save the last humans but ask for a price; thoughtful, uneasy and often recommended.

roots.title: Roots
roots.author: Alex Haley
roots.why: A family saga from an African village into American slavery; readers say it is one of the most powerful books they read.

girl next door.title: The Girl Next Door
girl next door.author: Jack Ketchum
girl next door.why: A teenager is tortured by her guardian and neighbourhood kids in 1950s suburbia; the book that broke readers, with an extremely disturbing story.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.author: Marilynne Robinson
gilead.why: An elderly minister writes a long letter to his young son; quiet, spiritual and beautifully written.

princess bride.title: The Princess Bride
princess bride.author: William Goldman
princess bride.why: A farm boy, a princess and a swordfight through fairy-tale perils; witty and loved even more than the movie.

wool.title: Wool
wool.author: Hugh Howey
wool.why: People live in an underground silo and the sheriff wants the truth; gripping with twists, and the basis of Silo.

jitterbug perfume.title: Jitterbug Perfume
jitterbug perfume.author: Tom Robbins
jitterbug perfume.why: A quest for the secret of immortality involving beets, perfume and gods; a funny, quirky book readers re-read yearly.

poppy war.title: The Poppy War
poppy war.author: R. F. Kuang
poppy war.why: A war orphan wins a place at an elite military school and discovers shamanic power; brutal, exceptional start to a series.

great believers.title: The Great Believers
great believers.author: Rebecca Makkai
great believers.why: Friends in 1980s Chicago face the AIDS crisis, and one's daughter searches for her family in 2015; left readers shattered.

pet sematary.title: Pet Sematary
pet sematary.author: Stephen King
pet sematary.why: A family finds a burial ground that brings the dead back; one of the bleakest King novels.

our wives under the sea.title: Our Wives Under the Sea
our wives under the sea.author: Julia Armfield
our wives under the sea.why: A wife returns from a deep-sea mission changed; short, strange and lyrical.

consider phlebas.title: Consider Phlebas
consider phlebas.author: Iain Banks
consider phlebas.why: A shape-shifter spy joins a war between the Culture and its enemies; big, action-driven space opera.

prince of tides.title: The Prince of Tides
prince of tides.author: Pat Conroy
prince of tides.why: A southern man confronts his family's secrets with his sister's psychiatrist; a long, emotional Southern novel.

awakening.title: The Awakening
awakening.author: Kate Chopin
awakening.why: A wife in 1890s Louisiana seeks independence; short and ahead of its time, and some readers say it changed their life.

king sorrow.title: King Sorrow
king sorrow.author: Joe Hill
king sorrow.why: The comments only say people are starting it, so there is no recommendation yet.

lies of locke lamora.title: The Lies of Locke Lamora
lies of locke lamora.author: Scott Lynch
lies of locke lamora.why: A gang of thieves in a Venice-like city gets pulled into a deadly plot; fast, funny fantasy heist and five-star read.

phantom tollbooth.title: The Phantom Tollbooth
phantom tollbooth.author: Norton Juster
phantom tollbooth.why: A bored boy drives into a land of puns and wordplay; clever, loved children's fantasy.

crying in h mart.title: Crying in H Mart
crying in h mart.author: Michelle Zauner
crying in h mart.why: The musician writes about losing her mother and her Korean heritage through food; moving and easy to read.

great gatsby.title: The Great Gatsby
great gatsby.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
great gatsby.why: A mysterious millionaire throws parties to win back his love in Jazz Age New York; short and beautifully written.

martian chronicles.title: The Martian Chronicles
martian chronicles.author: Ray Bradbury
martian chronicles.why: Linked stories about humans colonising Mars; lyrical and wistful rather than technical.

dutch house.title: The Dutch House
dutch house.author: Ann Patchett
dutch house.why: A brother and sister are cast out of their family mansion and remain obsessed with it; warm and gently moving.

priory of the orange tree.title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
priory of the orange tree.author: Samantha Shannon
priory of the orange tree.why: Dragons and queens in a standalone high fantasy with a sweeping plot; long but fast.

angelas ashes.title: Angela's Ashes
angelas ashes.author: Frank McCourt
angelas ashes.why: The author's poor Irish childhood in Limerick; sad and often darkly funny, and a bestselling memoir.

great expectations.title: Great Expectations
great expectations.author: Charles Dickens
great expectations.why: An orphan receives a mysterious fortune and learns what matters; one of the most readable Dickens novels.

pretty girls.title: Pretty Girls
pretty girls.author: Karin Slaughter
pretty girls.why: Two sisters uncover secrets about a serial killer; a gripping, graphic thriller that readers could not put down.

uprooted.title: Uprooted
uprooted.author: Naomi Novik
uprooted.why: A village girl is taken by a wizard to fight a corrupted wood; a fairy-tale inspired novel that gets absorbing.

sphere.title: Sphere
sphere.author: Michael Crichton
sphere.why: Scientists investigate a mysterious spacecraft on the ocean floor; long and gripping, though some find it minor Crichton.

emma.title: Emma
emma.author: Jane Austen
emma.why: A well-meaning matchmaker misreads everyone around her; light and witty, and free to read.

little big.title: Little, Big
little big.author: John Crowley
little big.why: A family's connection with fairies unfolds over generations; poetic and strange with a following.

hunger games.title: The Hunger Games
hunger games.author: Suzanne Collins
hunger games.why: A girl volunteers for a televised fight to the death; fast and gripping young-adult dystopia.

sapiens.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
sapiens.author: Yuval Noah Harari
sapiens.why: A broad history of humankind from the cognitive revolution on; readers call it excellent, though some dispute its science.

ministry for the future.title: The Ministry for the Future
ministry for the future.author: Kim Stanley Robinson
ministry for the future.why: A near-future institution works to fight climate change; ideas-heavy and told in many fragments, often recommended.

rejection.title: Rejection
rejection.author: Tony Tulathimutte
rejection.why: Linked stories about people rejected in love and in life; sharp, bold and laugh-out-loud.

night watch.title: Night Watch
night watch.author: Terry Pratchett
night watch.why: Sam Vimes is thrown back to his younger days during a revolt; often named the best Discworld book.

in the dream house.title: In the Dream House
in the dream house.author: Carmen Maria Machado
in the dream house.why: The author's memoir of an abusive relationship, told in short, shifting genre chapters; inventive and powerful.

guards guards.title: Guards! Guards!
guards guards.author: Terry Pratchett
guards guards.why: The Ankh-Morpork night watch faces a dragon; a funny, approachable start to the Watch series.

into the wild.title: Into the Wild
into the wild.author: Jon Krakauer
into the wild.why: The true story of a young man who went alone into Alaska; gripping and often recommended.

iliad.title: The Iliad
iliad.author: Homer
iliad.why: The wrath of Achilles during the siege of Troy; ancient and brutal epic that readers take on in a good translation.

eileen.title: Eileen
eileen.author: Ottessa Moshfegh
eileen.why: A lonely young woman working at a prison in 1960s New England meets a stranger; dark and sharp.

aurora.title: Aurora
aurora.author: Kim Stanley Robinson
aurora.why: One commenter hated it and another is unsure, so there is little clear recommendation.

dandelion wine.title: Dandelion Wine
dandelion wine.author: Ray Bradbury
dandelion wine.why: A boy's summer in 1928 small-town Illinois, full of wonder; nostalgic and lyrical, from a legitimate genius.

crying of lot 49.title: The Crying of Lot 49
crying of lot 49.author: Thomas Pynchon
crying of lot 49.why: A woman uncovers what may be a secret postal conspiracy in California; short, strange and a good first Pynchon.

power.title: The Power
power.author: Naomi Alderman
power.why: Women suddenly gain the ability to shock, flipping the balance of power; compelling and brutal.
